result.title: CaveBench: Benchmarking Abductive Physical Reasoning from Internal Observations
result.comment: 50 pages, 47 figures, 13 tables, including the appendix. Guanxin Lin and Chen Yang contributed equally. Chen Wang is the corresponding author. Project page: https://pier-lab.github.io/CaveBench/
result.summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) are advancing in physical reasoning, but whether they can understand external physical drivers from internal observations remains an open question. Existing benchmarks have not specifically targeted this setting. To this end, we introduce CaveBench, a benchmark for abductive physical reasoning from internal observations. Models receive apparatus descriptions and internal images while the external controls remain hidden, and must infer the operations responsible for the observed responses. CaveBench spans 20 apparatus scenes in five physical domains and contains 10,200 simulated episodes, split into 9,000 training, 1,000 validation, and 200 test episodes. Questions span one to six events and require the complete control set at every event, testing whether an explanation accounts for the entire process. Synchronized observations and control records provide the inputs and reference answers. Evaluating 27 VLM configurations yields six-event exact-match accuracies of 68.0% for the strongest closed-source model and 12.5% for the strongest open-weight model. Seven adaptation baselines show that single-event gains need not improve complete sequences. Error analysis identifies failures in visual identification, physical inference, evidence integration, and action composition, specifying where current models struggle to connect internal phenomena with their external causes.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 CaveBench：模型只能看到装置描述与内部观测图像，外部控制隐藏，需反推导致观测响应的操作；含 5 个物理域、20 个场景、10,200 条模拟 episode，问题覆盖 1–6 个事件且要求给出完整控制集，并评测 27 种 VLM 配置与 7 个适配基线。
AI.relevance_reason: 属于视觉证据到因果解释的诊断型基准，其「单事件提升未必迁移到完整序列」及视觉识别、物理推断、证据整合、动作组合四类失败，可供核查多事件推理中证据筛选与状态累积的瓶颈。
